rules.rationale: Multiple N/O sites donate and accept hydrogen bonds to water, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Few polar sites still add favorable solute-water contacts without burying them under a large apolar scaffold.
Halogen-rich solutes are apolar and poorly solvated; polarizability alone does not offset the loss of hydrogen bonding.
Fused aromatic scaffolds are flat and hydrophobic; pi density is weakly hydrating versus polar substituent groups.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the polarity mechanism that won on development seeds, adding an aromatic-apolar penalty to sharpen the low end. It fails if aromatic species with polar substituents occupy the top of the hydration pool.

rules.rationale: Reverses the uncertain source ring prior: rigid polycyclic solutes pack apolar surface and solvate poorly in water.
Acyclic and heteroatom-free together mark pure hydrocarbons, whose hydration is entropically costly despite the acyclic bonus.
Highly branched skeletons raise hydrophobic surface area and reduce favorable water contact per heavy atom.
Unsaturated centers often accompany carbonyl and imine groups, which are strong hydration acceptors.

skills.hypothesis: Tests whether ring topology and unsaturation proxy hydrogen-bonding capacity, downweighting the high-transfer-weight source ring relation. It fails if ring presence genuinely tracks favorable hydration in the top pool.

state.lesson: The polarity mechanism generalized strongly across all eight development seeds (mean AUC ~83 versus ~51 for the transferred ESOL size prior), so refinements should keep heteroatom and halogen polarity terms central and treat source length and ring relations as low-confidence priors.
state.revision_summary: Kept the deployed polarity core, replacing the short-plus-apolar interaction term with an aromatic-apolar penalty and slightly relaxing semantic mass decay. Proposes a complementary counter-skill that reverses the high-transfer-weight ring relation and adds branch, ring, and unsaturation topology terms as hydrogen-bonding proxies, and retains the polarity core for deployment.
